long_biography.plain_text:
Painting was Nicola Muciaccia's first ambition, but illness caused by artists' materials forced him to change direction. He began in the warehouse of Italian carrier Bartolini, devised a color-coding method for shipments and rose to commercial director. A glimpse of containers moving between rail and road in Belgium then suggested a different logistics model. In 1977, he founded his own transport company in Bari.

That venture became GTS, an integrated logistics group built around intermodal freight. Muciaccia remained closely identified with its shift from relying on outside rail operators to controlling more of the transport chain. The group later expanded its locomotives, wagons, containers and maintenance capacity, serving routes across Europe. Executive leadership passed to his son Alessio, while Muciaccia continued as president and a holding-company director, preserving a founder's role as the business entered its second generation.
